title: Resolve grounding conflicts via per-field max, not `ours` unconditionally
context: Hard git conflicts confined to the counts sentence in Hunch grounding files were being resolved by always keeping `ours`. But if `theirs` carries a higher count (e.g., 243 decisions vs 241), that higher count may be the ahead-of-store signal fnd_6391b4242f depends on — a phantom record the branch claimed but the store never received. Unconditionally discarding it loses that signal. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: When a counts-only conflict is detected, resolve it to the element-wise max of each field (decisions, bugs, constraints, etc.) across both sides, rather than picking `ours` outright. If ours has `241 decisions, 5 bugs` and theirs has `243 decisions, 2 bugs`, the resolution becomes `243 decisions, 5 bugs`. Extracted a shared `renderCountsMatch()` function (used by both doc generator and merge driver) to prevent drift.
consequences: Higher counts from either side survive the merge instead of being silently discarded
Ahead-of-store signals are preserved when one side carries a phantom count
Post-merge refresh hooks still function as a safety net for further refinement
Code now has a single source of truth for counts sentence formatting, eliminating divergence risk
Test coverage expanded to verify per-field max behavior and phantom-record scenarios
alternatives_rejected: Keep `ours` unconditionally (prior approach; loses higher count signal)
Use heuristic averaging or other logic (semantically wrong for append-only counts)
Require manual resolution (conflicts in automated merge drivers should be minimal)
